title: release step 1 fails with an empty detail when the tag listed last matches the template and names no version
body:
## What happens

`release` stops at step 1 with an empty detail when the tag git lists LAST matches the release template but names no X.Y.Z version. It fails a relative target (`--patch`) and an explicit one (`v1.2.3`) alike.

Found at Utilz (utilz-vc, confirmed by vc). Its template is `{version}` and its old `v2.6.1` tag is listed after every `2.x.y`, so every cut of Utilz failed step 1 and said nothing.

## Why

`release_versions` (lib/release.steps) ended its loop body with `is_semver "$v" && printf ...`. A loop's status is its last body's, so a last tag that is not a version made the loop exit 1. Under pipefail, which every handler sets, that became the pipeline's status. `release_resolve` then returned 1, and nothing had warned.

git lists tags in byte order, so which tag comes last is an accident of spelling. A `v1.0.0-rc1` beside `v1.0.0` does it under the default template `v{version}` too.

## Fix (default, no override needed: this is a defect, not a policy)

1. The test is an `if`: `if is_semver "$v"; then printf ...; fi`. The loop's status no longer depends on which tag is last.
2. No silent failure: `release_versions` warns on every path that returns non-zero. It already did when git cannot list the tags; it now also warns when the versions cannot be sorted, naming the template. Every other failure out of `release_resolve` already names itself, so step 1 never fails with an empty detail.

## Tests (red first)

In tests/unit/releasecut.bats:
- A `v1.0.0-rc1` tag listed after `v1.0.0`: `--patch` and `v1.0.1` both resolve to 1.0.1.
- Utilz's shape, template `{version}` with `v1.0.0` listed after `1.0.0`: `--patch` and `1.0.1` both resolve.
- Every failure path of `release_versions` warns: outside a repository it names the tag listing; with `sort` refusing it names the sort.


## Resolution

Fixed at `549030e`, the new arms driven red first at its parent. Reviewed by vc with mutants in scratch copies: the `if` reverted to `is_semver && printf` kills arms 1 and 2; the sort-failure warn dropped kills arm 3. Full suite 1585/1585 at `96ec3db`, 0 not ok, 3 machine-bound skips as at 0.1.4 (tmp/test/20260921-2100.bats.*), run with no GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS in the environment. Ships in 0.1.5.
